claims.claim: **SVT is common in infancy and childhood**, usually re-entrant, in otherwise well children. **Over one third of new-onset SVT starts in the first few weeks of life**, often presenting after many hours with heart failure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Younger children: usually AVRT** (including Wolff-Parkinson-White). **Adolescents: more often AVNRT.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SVT has a fixed rate, usually over 220 bpm**, with abrupt onset and offset; P-waves are not visible or sit after the QRS.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat a broad-complex tachycardia as VT** (rather than SVT with aberrancy) unless it is clearly shown not to be VT.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for and address contributors**: sepsis, pain, dehydration, anxiety and fever.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infants tolerate it well and present late** — irritability, poor feeding, lethargy, sweating, then congestive heart failure. **Older children feel palpitations and present earlier**, often with a normal examination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Recognise shock** (hypotension, pallor, poor perfusion, decreased consciousness) **and resuscitate at once.** Red flags: unwell appearance, hypotension, drowsiness. **BP machines and oximeters may be unreliable at SVT rates.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **12-lead ECG before and after reversion.** CXR only if heart failure signs; **blood tests are not recommended** unless considering other causes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sinus tachycardia:** under 220, normal P-waves, variable rate, unwell child. **SVT:** over 220 (commonly 250–300 in infants), P-waves absent or after the QRS, fixed rate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Atrial flutter** reaches up to 500/min in neonates (300/min in children); sawtooth waves are often seen only with adenosine-induced AV block. **Atrial ectopic tachycardia** can fail to respond to adenosine or DC cardioversion, and can cause cardiomyopathy. **Junctional ectopic tachycardia** (rate 170–300) occurs after cardiac surgery.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Only in a clinically stable child, on continuous cardiac monitoring.** If unsuccessful or the child deteriorates, move to medical treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do NOT use eyeball pressure or carotid sinus massage.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Under 6 months: immerse the face in ice water for 5 seconds** (diving reflex) — no need to occlude the nostrils; safe and 90% effective.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never use facial immersion in an infant with haemodynamic compromise or shock.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Older infants and toddlers:** hold an ice-cold facecloth or a bag of ice slurry on the face for 15–30 seconds.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **School-aged children: Valsalva** — lying supine, take a full breath in, then blow into a thumb or a 10 mL syringe for 10–15 seconds, straining visibly without letting air escape.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Modified Valsalva is more effective:** strain semi-recumbent, then lie flat immediately with passive leg raise to 45 degrees.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adenosine's half-life is 5–10 seconds**; it briefly blocks the AV node. **Always record a rhythm strip during it** — the response helps diagnosis even if SVT doesn't terminate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Flushing and chest tightness are common.** ⚠️ **It can exacerbate asthma — avoid with a history of severe asthma or active wheeze.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lower dose with dipyridamole; avoid if possible after cardiac transplant** (asystole, bradycardia — lower dose and consult cardiology if used). **Children on theophylline need higher doses** — consult cardiology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Adenosine can turn re-entry SVT into atrial fibrillation — dangerous with WPW, needs DC cardioversion.** Rapid re-initiation is not uncommon; discuss with cardiology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Verapamil is contraindicated under 12 months** (irreversible hypotension, lethal ventricular dysfunction) and is not routinely used in children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Often needs admission:** first presentation · under 3 months · heart failure · needed DC conversion.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Known SVT with a breakthrough episode:** discuss with the child's usual cardiology team.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge once reverted, not meeting admission criteria, and observed for 90 minutes**, with follow-up arranged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23
